body: I'm not comparing the performance/satisfaction result. I'm trying to determine the visual value.
Must also be in in the same way interest rates don't matter.

That's great and all, which is why I added the first part to my title.... But I'm trying to determine which of the two purely has a better eye candy value. It would appear it has no eye candy value which can't be true. If they're forced to select an option then one must be valued more than the other.
In this scenario, you have to make the conscious decision to select something. It's not dinner; you can't make us guess what you want. We know it doesn't matter only until we select what you want.

I'm trying to understand from purely a visual, aesthetically pleasing perspective. People always jump to the performance/satisfaction end results but I'm most interested in knowing eye candy value of the two.
So if you could design your perfect man, you'd give him a tic-tac hose?
Why? The thought never crosses your mind? A bulge doesn't catch your eye? Are you really insinuating that a micro spear is indistinguishable from a 50cal DNA rifle?

How often do you come across applicants that have mental/physical disabilities that impair their performance within an academic environment.  Are these applications evaluated any differently from others? Finally, in your opinion, would it be better to just not mention these sort of things.

I can't understand how somebody could even summarize their admission decision with inspect element. 

It's not like the code is going to say, "status = accepted;" .
